items.prompt: GET /api/tickets/:id hides internal notes from a VIEWER. How can a viewer still read them?
items.answer: By PATCHing tags, whose write response returns every comment unfiltered
distractors: By requesting the ticket list, which carries each row's full comment thread
They cannot, as a Prisma middleware filters comment visibility on all queries
By posting an internal note, which echoes back the ticket's hidden notes
items.explanation: Only getTicket overrides the comments include with visibleCommentWhere; write responses reuse the raw include (finding 1).

items.prompt: A request reaches /api/tickets with no x-tenant-slug or x-user-email header. Who is it treated as?
items.answer: As agent@acme.test in acme-support, the defaults for missing headers
distractors: As nobody, so it gets a 401 when both identity headers are missing
As a read-only viewer, the safest default role for an anonymous caller
As the first admin user of the first tenant, ordered by creation date
items.explanation: Header-based demo auth with defaults means an anonymous request is an agent: intentionally temporary, but worth knowing.

items.prompt: An agent PATCHes a NEW ticket to CLOSED. Which status code comes back, and why?
items.answer: 500, because the domain throws a plain Error, not an HttpError
distractors: 409, the conventional conflict response for an invalid status transition
403, because agents may never close tickets from any status at all
400 from Zod, because CLOSED fails the status enum in the PATCH schema
items.explanation: assertTicketTransition throws a plain Error, and the error middleware maps only ZodError (400) and HttpError (its status) to client codes; everything else becomes 500. Throw an HttpError(409) or map a domain error class instead.

items.prompt: From which statuses may an AGENT move a ticket to CLOSED?
items.answer: Only from RESOLVED or PENDING, a special case checked before the table
distractors: From OPEN, PENDING or RESOLVED, the same as any other role may do
From no status at all, as closing a ticket is reserved for managers and admins
From any status, as agents bypass the shared transition table
items.explanation: canTransitionTicket special-cases to === CLOSED for agents before consulting the shared table (which also allows OPEN -> CLOSED for others).

items.prompt: A VIEWER sends PATCH with status equal to the ticket's current status. Does assertTicketTransition stop it?
items.answer: No, since from === to returns true before the viewer check runs
distractors: Yes, since viewers can never send a status field in a PATCH request
Yes, since the domain package rejects every same-status move
Only when the ticket is CLOSED, since closed tickets are frozen
items.explanation: Order of checks matters: the identity shortcut comes first, so a viewer's no-op status passes.

items.prompt: Two tickets are created concurrently in the same tenant. What can happen?
items.answer: Both pick the same next number, and the second fails the unique index with 500
distractors: Nothing, as the transaction serializes the two highest-number reads
Both succeed with duplicate numbers, as number has no unique index
The second silently gets number + 2 through an automatic retry
items.explanation: Reading 'highest + 1' inside a READ COMMITTED transaction does not reserve the number; use a sequence/counter row or retry on conflict.

items.prompt: The database is unreachable for one polling pass, so findMany throws. What happens to the worker?
items.answer: Polling stops for good, as the loop rejects before the next setTimeout
distractors: It retries the same pass once the configured poll interval has elapsed
It marks every pending event FAILED and then carries on polling
Node restarts the worker process automatically after the unhandled crash
items.explanation: The loop's promise rejects before setTimeout schedules the next pass; only per-event errors are caught. Wrapping processOutboxBatch in try/catch and always rescheduling keeps the worker alive.

items.prompt: One worker is running and 15 outbox events are PENDING. Which of them does a single polling pass process?
items.answer: The 10 oldest by createdAt; the other 5 wait for the next pass
distractors: All 15, as the loop keeps reading until no PENDING rows remain
The 10 newest by createdAt; the most recent changes go out first
Any 10 of them, as findMany here returns rows in no fixed order
items.explanation: processOutboxBatch runs findMany with where status PENDING, orderBy createdAt asc and take: 10, then handles only that batch before the loop waits.

items.prompt: WORKER_POLL_INTERVAL_MS is not set. How long does the worker wait between polling passes, and when does that wait start?
items.answer: 4 seconds, counted from when the previous batch has finished
distractors: 10 seconds, as the worker falls back to a ten-second interval
1 second, the default interval when the variable is unset
5 seconds; the wait starts the moment the previous pass was scheduled
items.explanation: pollIntervalMs is Number(process.env.WORKER_POLL_INTERVAL_MS ?? 4000). loop() awaits processOutboxBatch() and only then calls setTimeout(loop, pollIntervalMs), so the 4000 ms starts after the batch completes.

items.prompt: What classic bug does writing an OutboxEvent in the same transaction as the ticket change prevent?
items.answer: A saved change whose notification is lost with no record it was owed
distractors: Two agents editing the same ticket at the same moment and colliding
Customers getting their notification emails rendered in the wrong zone
The worker reading uncommitted ticket data from another transaction
items.explanation: Writing the OutboxEvent in the same transaction means the change and its pending side effect commit or roll back together; the classic bug is a DB write that succeeds while the notification fails before anything records that it still needs sending.

items.prompt: A NORMAL ticket created 20 hours ago is raised to URGENT. When is it now due?
items.answer: Two hours from now, as slaDueAt is reset from the current time
distractors: Already breached, as two hours after creation was 18 hours ago
Still 4 hours from now, because the original NORMAL deadline is kept
Two hours from the last customer reply, which restarts the clock
items.explanation: When the priority changes, updateTicket recalculates slaDueAt with calculateSlaDueAt(new Date(), priority), i.e. from now, not from creation.

items.prompt: Two agents post the first public reply at the same moment. Why can firstResponseAt be overwritten?
items.answer: It is read before the transaction, so both see null and both write it
distractors: Prisma drops the WHERE firstResponseAt IS NULL guard; the update runs anyway
Internal notes also set firstResponseAt when they are the first comment
It cannot, as the comment insert locks the ticket row until commit
items.explanation: The check is outside the transaction and the update is unconditional by id; a conditional update (where firstResponseAt: null) would make the first writer win.

items.front: Which write actions are open to a VIEWER in the support desk?
items.back: Creating tickets, changing priority or tags, posting public replies to customers and ingesting email. Only status changes and assignment are checked; requireRole guards just the audit-log route.

PENDING, RESOLVED and CLOSED are PAUSED; no due date is MET; past due is BREACHED; within one hour of due is AT_RISK; otherwise MET. Leaving PENDING keeps the original slaDueAt, so paused time still counts.

items.front: Two upgrades that make the outbox worker production-shaped
items.back: Retry: add availableAt and select status in (PENDING, FAILED) with attempts < 5 and availableAt <= now. Claim: UPDATE ... SET status = 'PROCESSING' WHERE id IN (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED LIMIT 10) RETURNING * so concurrent workers never share an event.

items.front: What happens to the domain package's visibility rule in practice?
items.back: canViewInternalNote and canManageUsers exist but are unused; the visibility rule is re-implemented inline in visibleCommentWhere, so the domain package and the service can drift apart.
